context.text:
Joint causal-SLO-externality P/D placement. The decision rule is a joint
argmin over (decode endpoint d, prefill placement p) of

    J(d, p) = V * ( externality(d, p) - ownGood(d, p) ),   V = 8

with the capacity term disabled (the `causal_externality_no_capacity_v8`
controller, config.md §9.2). Candidates are priced by the smooth SLO value
they destroy among their residents, evaluated causally: every completion
model is gated on an admission window, so a resident finishing before the
arrival is admitted contributes exactly zero. That gating is what makes the
term an externality rather than another load proxy, and it is why the effect
survives on a fleet whose load signals are already balanced.

REQUIRED SHAPE -- a joint argmin over the cross product: D local candidates
plus D*P disaggregated candidates, scored on one scale in one argmin. This
CANNOT be a per-endpoint Scorer at this pin, for two independent reasons: a
scorer returns a per-endpoint map, so no pair can be named; and every scorer
contribution passes through the profile's score-range enforcement, which
clamps to [0,1], while J is signed and unbounded -- clamping collapses every
candidate with J <= 0 to one score, destroying the ranking rather than
degrading it. The comparator faces the same hazard for a different reason:
its objective is a latency in microseconds, non-negative and unbounded above.

PLACEMENT -- TWO plugin registrations sharing state, not one plugin with two
interfaces. ProfileHandler.Pick and Picker.Pick share a method name with
different signatures (pkg/epp/framework/interface/scheduling/plugins.go:47,
:77), so no single Go type can satisfy both:

  Handler: ProfileHandler (Pick, ProcessResults) + PreRequest +
          ResponseBodyProcessor
  Picker:  Filter + Picker

Filter is required, not incidental: Picker.Pick receives only
[]*ScoredEndpoint and no request, so the arriving request's token count
reaches the argmin no other way. All profiles receive the same
candidateEndpoints slice (pkg/epp/scheduling/scheduler.go:78), so an
unfiltered profile sees both pools; ProfileRunResult.TargetEndpoints is a
slice (pkg/epp/framework/interface/scheduling/types.go:165-167), so one
picker run carries both picks.

THE HAZARD IS SILENT FALLBACK to the target's natural decode-first
decomposition: pick a decode endpoint with the stock scorer, then decide
placement. That is the simulation's decode-first ablation arm, so its cost is
measured rather than estimated -- +0.0485 equal-cell mean goodput in favour of
the joint shape, 95% CI [+0.0305, +0.0665], worst cell falling 0.918 -> 0.700
at h100_a100_realistic:interactive:medium_0p80. A port that keeps the stock
handler and moves J into a binary disaggregate() gate still runs, still
reports goodput, and is running a different algorithm. The decomposition
switch is kept reachable (config.md §10) because flipping it is the cheapest
on-cluster check that the joint shape survived the port.

Three settings are forced on an internal copy of the decider rather than
exposed as flags, so a port must hard-wire them: exact prefill overlap,
deployable resident estimates (censored N_out, never true remaining), and
collocated-prefill pricing (config.md §9.2).

THETA IS KEYED BY POD LABEL, NOT BY THE SCENARIO (config.md §5 signal 8, §2).
Per-GPU coefficients differ most in the per-iteration intercept -- 25 563.82 us
on A100 against 16 613.54 us on H100, a factor of 1.539 present on EVERY
iteration regardless of KV state -- so a wrong or defaulted GPU label is wrong
on every decision. Reject absent or unknown types; never default. Both
coefficient files must be transcribed into every arm's plugin config, keyed by
label value, so the A100 decode instance is priced correctly whether or not the
generated scenario names it.

FLEET CAPABILITY GAP, disclosed not silent (config.md §2). The campaign's
decode pool is genuinely heterogeneous -- instance_1 on H100, instance_2 on
A100 -- and that heterogeneity is the condition the mechanism exploits. The
scenario schema expresses one acceleratorType per role and has no construct
for per-instance hardware within a role, so the generated baseline names H100
for both roles and describes only instance_1. The A100 decode pod must be
deployed outside the generated scenario or the scenario hand-edited. This
bundle deliberately does not choose among config.md §2's options.

DECLARED DEGRADATION (D1): every cited margin was produced with the
scheduler-rollout TTFT model, whose per-request wait-queue inputs are
unobtainable at this pin -- the target exposes WaitingQueueSize, one integer.
The port substitutes the closed-form rollforward estimator, which past one
batch drain understates admission delay and so biases toward remote prefill.
A substitution counter is required, not optional: the fallback is acceptable,
the silence is the defect. Net direction across all declared degradations is
NOT known and is NOT claimed -- D1 biases remote, D2b and D2c bias local.
See README.md, "Pre-registered expectation" and "Open threats to validity".
